section_summary: The section ends a translated Japanese budget for fiscal year 1941–42, including multiyear subsidies, government guarantees, and spending commitments for transport, industry, defense, and overseas administrations. An extra budget follows. The remaining documents report Japanese banking activity, trade credits, financial controls, and the proposed shipment of bonds to Japan in 1941.

subfiles.title: Japanese budget commitments for fiscal year 1941–42, continued
subfiles.about: Lists multiyear expenditure commitments, subsidies, indemnities, and guarantees across Japanese departments and overseas administrations.
subfiles.summary: The continuation covers public works, military procurement, export and industrial assistance, shipping and aviation subsidies, and special account purchases. It sets route and aircraft conditions for subsidized air services and gives terms for tank vessel subsidies and shipbuilding loans. Later pages detail commitments by the Governments-General of Korea and Taiwan, including air routes, irrigation, reclamation, coal, and trade.

subfiles.title: Extra Budget for 1941–42 Fiscal Year
subfiles.about: Authorizes further commitments for foreign exchange, supplies, trade, industry, marine insurance, and aviation.
subfiles.summary: Published in the Official Gazette, the extra budget authorizes substantial indemnities for foreign exchange, wartime marine insurance, munitions materials, and industrial activity. It also funds fertilizers, export development, Northern Sakhalin oil and coal interests, and a Tokyo–Saigon–Bangkok air service.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Financial and Economic Annual of Japan, 1940
subfiles.about: Transmits two copies of Japan’s fortieth Financial and Economic Annual.
subfiles.summary: Requests distribution of the two annuals to Joseph M. Jones and the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.

subfiles.title: Transfers from Bank of Java account to Yokohama Specie Bank
subfiles.about: Reports three transfers totaling $14 million from the Bank of Java to the Yokohama Specie Bank.
subfiles.summary: Treasury will watch for further Japanese withdrawals from Java.

subfiles.title: Payments to Robert Jickey
subfiles.about: Reports six April payments totaling $212,000 to Robert Jickey through Chase National Bank.
subfiles.summary: Payments were ordered by Japan Cotton Company and charged to Yokohama Specie Bank, New York.

subfiles.title: Deposit to Yokohama Specie Bank account
subfiles.about: Reports a May 22 deposit to the bank’s New York account from two insurance companies.
subfiles.summary: Checks from Meiji and Tokyo Marine and Fire insurers comprised nearly all of the $4.75 million deposit.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal of Japanese cash credit memorandum
subfiles.about: Forwards information on cash credits established by Japanese firms in New York.
subfiles.summary: Introduces the attached July 1 memorandum.

subfiles.title: Cash credits at National City Bank of New York
subfiles.about: Lists Japanese and Thai commercial credits for metals, oil, aircraft engines, railway cars, and other goods.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum identifies credits opened by Japanese firms and the Thai Commercial Bank. It gives amounts, suppliers, destinations, commodities, and further bank findings on several transactions.

subfiles.title: Bankers Trust financing of imported Japanese silver
subfiles.about: Explains Bankers Trust’s financing of Baker and Company silver imported from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Emerson says the financing begins after the silver reaches the United States.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Specie Bank cash withdrawals
subfiles.about: Reports three New York cash withdrawals by Yokohama Specie Bank in May 1941.
subfiles.summary: Withdrawals totaled $100,000, all in $100 bills.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Specie Bank cashier’s check for silver
subfiles.about: Reports a $293,000 cashier’s check connected to a silver shipment for Baker and Company.
subfiles.summary: The check was bought in San Francisco and covered silver presumed shipped from Japan.

subfiles.title: Japanese plan to revise national financial structure
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese plan to expand Bank of Japan control over financial institutions.
subfiles.summary: The plan also proposes changes to capital mobilization, accounting, budgets, and taxes.

subfiles.title: National City Bank facilities for Axis banks and firms
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum concerning banking facilities for German, Italian, and Japanese clients.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to the original Treasury paper.

subfiles.title: Japanese dollar account at Bank of Brazil
subfiles.about: Reports deposits and urgent Japanese requests for letters of credit through the Bank of Brazil.
subfiles.summary: Japanese representatives deposited $2 million and sought credits for hides and other Latin American exports to Japan. Brazil’s Director of Exchange refused a proposed credit for explosives from Spain via Argentina.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Rio de Janeiro telegram on Japanese banking
subfiles.about: Paraphrases Caffery’s report on Japanese Bank of Brazil transactions.
subfiles.summary: It repeats the $2 million deposit, export credits, and refusal of a credit for Spanish explosives destined for Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Rio de Janeiro telegram paraphrase
subfiles.about: Encloses six copies of the paraphrased telegram about Japan’s Bank of Brazil dollar account.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the Rio de Janeiro report.

subfiles.title: Indochina loan for Japanese military expenditures
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram reporting Vichy’s agreement to an Indochina loan for Japanese military costs.
subfiles.summary: The reported loan was one million piastres.

subfiles.title: FBI transmittal concerning proposed bond shipment
subfiles.about: Forwards an FBI memorandum on a proposed $5 million bond shipment to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Notes prior discussion with Fred Lyon and copies sent to Army and Navy intelligence.

subfiles.title: Proposed shipment of bonds aboard Tatuta Maru
subfiles.about: Reports a planned armored car transfer of $5 million in bonds to a ship bound for Japan.
subfiles.summary: S. Uno reportedly arranged the shipment and requested secrecy.

subfiles.title: Treatment of Japanese officials and accounts
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on Japanese officials’ accounts and Americans’ situation in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a frozen credits telegram.

subfiles.title: Restricted item withdrawal notice
subfiles.about: Records the removal of a restricted item from the file.
subfiles.summary: Identifies item 894.51/730 as withdrawn for restricted information.

subfiles.title: Frozen funds and bank withdrawals in Chefoo
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on freezing regulations and restrictions on employers’ bank withdrawals.
subfiles.summary: British and American employers reportedly could not withdraw funds to pay workers.
